## 59a9a5c505fb

### A-59-1 — reproduced distribution shortcut: complete nested frames only

Across 200 draws in each of easy, medium, and hard (600 total), every component was a complete rectangle frame, every sequence of bounding boxes was strictly nested, and a “fill complete frames, otherwise count only visible cells” rival matched 600/600 intended outputs. The same rival also matched all 5 canonical pairs, all of which were complete strictly nested frames. Evidence: `checks/audit/audit-probe.json` and `checks/audit/probe.py`.

The retained counterexample `checks/audit/59a9a5c505fb/input.json` contains two connected non-frame L-shaped objects with overlapping bounding boxes. It **passes the target validator but is outside the default generator distribution**. The live Racket fills/counts both full bounding boxes (`checks/audit/59a9a5c505fb/racket.json`), while the frame-only rival leaves non-frame interiors unfilled (`checks/audit/59a9a5c505fb/rival-output.json`). The outputs differ, so the generated/canonical data do not distinguish the general bbox rule from the shortcut. The supported apply command exited 0; its log is `checks/audit/59a9a5c505fb/apply-command.log`.

No source change was made to this audit target.
